changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7658-toc-code-span-anchor-parity.md`

- names `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx` → `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx` — edited by this change

  > Seven live headings in this repo's own docs were affected (`content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`, `content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx`, `packages/cli/README.md`). Pinned against the real render pipeline rather than a second derivation of the slug rules: the new test renders each heading through `MarkdownImpl` and compares `extractToc`'s id to the `id` attribute `rehype-slug` actually emitted.

Pinned against the real render pipeline rather than a second derivation of the slug rules: the new test renders each heading through `MarkdownImpl` and compares `extractToc`'s id to the `id` attribute `rehype-slug` actually emitted.

### `.changeset/7694-chart-series-chart-type-alias-refusal.md`

- names `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` → `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` — edited by this change

  > - **Before:** `series: [{ name: 'revenue', chartType: 'line' }]` validated green through `@object-ui/types/zod` (`safeValidateSchema`, `objectui check` / `objectui validate`, any pipeline that keeps `parse()`'s output) — and the key was gone from the output, so a consumer of the parse result drew that series in the chart's own family, precisely what the author was overriding. On the TypeScript face the key was merely an excess property on a fresh literal; a widened object carrying it assigned structurally. - **After:** the same document REFUSES at `series[i].chartType` (issue code `invalid_type`) with one message on both channels — the parse-time issue and the `.describe()` metadata: `Unrecognized key(s) on this chart series: \`chartType\`. Did you mean \`chartType\` → \`type\`? …` followed by the reason and the remedy. Write `type: 'bar' | 'line' | 'area'`. On the TypeScript face `ChartDataSeries.chartType` is a `?: never` tombstone, so both the fresh literal and the widened assignment are `tsc` errors. - **Both written** (`{ type: 'bar', chartType: 'line' }`) is refused at `chartType` alone — the key is not folded onto `type` and no precedence is minted between the two spellings. - **Which documents to scan.** The narrowing does not stop at `ChartDataSeriesSchema`; it reaches every document through the parents that embed it — `ChartSchema.series` (`zod/data-display.zod.ts`, `z.array(ChartDataSeriesSchema)`) and, one level further out, `ReportSectionSchema.chart` (`zod/reports.zod.ts`, `ChartSchema.optional()`). Authors meet it through `safeValidateSchema()` (`zod/index.zod.ts`, which parses `AnyComponentSchema`) and through the CLI's `objectui validate` command (`packages/cli/src/cli.ts`). In practice: every `chart` node's `series[]`, and every report section whose `chart` carries one.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `fcdc8ec91` (merge-base with origin/main): 10 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 2048 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2677 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/37065230018)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a20223743cba4e8962bed892a5b06fe166afa799`
Local-runs: none
Rendered: 2026-10-02T21:37Z

PR objectui#11508 (card objectui#11500), judged against triage's ruling `5960445419` (retire `create plugin`, `lint` / `test` and `studio`; the four noted residues as one-line corrections, each to what the command does; refusal pins plus the objectui#11496 enumeration pin), on the family's precedents: PR objectui#11499's record `5959693747`, PR objectui#11495's `5958276867` and PR objectui#11487's `5957439389`. Read for this record: the card body and all four comments on it (the ruling, the claim `5961116498`, the dev report `5961579588` read as a claim to test, and the seat's ACCEPT `5961728905` read the same way); the PR body and its 11-file list; the net diff of the head against `main` (merge-base `fcdc8ec91`..head, +140 / −406 over `.changeset/11500-retire-cli-create-lint-test-studio.md`, `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`, `packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/cli/src/__tests__/cli-bin.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/analyze.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`, and the deleted `commands/create-plugin.ts`, `lint.ts`, `studio.ts`, `test.ts`; `main` has since moved one commit to `9d9ed5495`, PR objectui#11502, whose diff over `packages/cli` touches only `utils/known-schema-types.ts` and `registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts`, and the three-dot diff against current `main` is byte-identical to the merge-base diff); and the check-runs on the head, read twice more than a minute apart, the set complete at both reads. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally: the head's tree is read with `git show` / `git grep` against the fetched ref, the dev's reverse-verification legs are read as reported, and the head's own check-runs are the gate verdicts. Placeholders are spelled in capitals (`NAME`, `UNKNOWN`, `COMPONENT`) because the body sanitizer strips angle-bracket shapes.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The published bin's accept set narrows by four commands — right.** `cli.ts` at the head declares ten `.command(` entries (`serve dev build start init generate doctor check validate analyze`) and imports none of the four modules; the four files are deleted, not stubbed. `packages/cli/src` sets no `allowUnknownOption`, `passThroughOptions`, `allowExcessArguments`, `enablePositionalOptions` or `exitOverride` (grep at the head: none), and the CLI runs commander `^15`, whose default refuses an undeclared first token with `error: unknown command 'NAME'` and a non-zero exit before any action runs — for `create plugin probe-widget` the refused token is `create`. So each retirement is a refusal, not a silent accept, and nothing is written. `plugin` was the only `type` the deleted `create` action accepted, so retiring `create` whole is the ruling's unit. No dependency was added: `packages/cli/package.json` is not in the diff, which is the ruling's ⛔.
2. **The enumeration pin's new declared set — right.** `SUBCOMMANDS` in `cli-bin.test.ts` is those same ten names in the same order; the pin still reads commander's `Commands:` section both directions (set equality, no duplicates, `help` as the lit control). A retired command coming back fails this pin before its own refusal pin does, which the dev's restore-one leg shows (2 failed: enumeration plus the `studio` refusal).
3. **The four refusal pins — right.** One `it.each` over `create plugin probe-widget`, `lint`, `test`, `studio`: exit non-zero, stderr contains `unknown command 'NAME'`, the temp directory stays empty, and the control is the same directory answering `g page Probe` with exit 0 and exactly `pages`, `pages/probe.json`. These runs spawn `process.execPath` with `PATH` emptied, so the node binary still resolves while a resurrected `studio` or `lint` would die at its first external tool instead of starting a dev server from inside the suite — a sound guard, and the reason the BASE leg's `studio` failed on `pnpm: not found` rather than on a port. `cli-bin.test.ts` self-builds `dist/cli.js` when absent and is a `*.test.ts` file, so it is judged by the eight `Test (shard N/8)` runs, not by `Test (dist pins)` (`pnpm test:dist`, the `*.dist.spec.tsx` project).
4. **`analyze` without `dist/` now exits non-zero — right.** `analyzeBundleSize()` throws `No dist/ directory to analyze. Run \`objectui build\` first.` where it used to print a warning and `return`; `analyze()` has no catch, so the throw reaches the `analyze` action's existing catch in `cli.ts`, which prints `Error:` plus the message on stderr and calls `process.exit(1)`; `✓ Analysis complete!` sits after the `await` and never prints. The two banner lines still print on stdout first, which the PR's Acceptance notes say and which no pin or script reads as a pass. The pin asserts exit non-zero, `dist/` on stderr, no `analysis complete` on stdout, and an empty tree. With a `dist/`, the report is unchanged (the objectui#11496 control pin is untouched). The docs sentence "With no `dist/` to analyze, it exits non-zero" matches.
5. **`init NAME --template UNKNOWN` refuses before the directory exists — right.** `const files = buildInitFiles(name, options.template)` is now evaluated after the already-exists check and before `mkdirSync(projectDir, …)`; `buildInitFiles` throws `Unknown template: UNKNOWN` for a name outside `templates`, and the `init` action's catch exits 1. The `name === '.'` path never made a directory and is unchanged; the file map and write order are unchanged (the byte-for-byte pin over `buildInitFiles` still holds). The deleted comment "Unknown templates still throw here, before the first write" was true of files and false of the directory, and is corrected. The pin asserts exit non-zero, `unknown template` on stderr, an empty tree, then the same directory scaffolding `probe-app/app.json` with `-t simple`. The change is one hoisted statement (+1 line, the loop header 3 lines to 1, one comment), which the ruling allows when "named in the report" — it is named in the report, the PR body and the changeset.
6. **The `doctor` text corrections — right.** The help line becomes `Diagnose common project setup issues (reports only, changes nothing)`; `doctor.ts` at the head reads files and `console.log`s findings, writes nothing, and reads no `process.version`, so both the old "and fix" and the old docs promise of a "Node version" check were claims with no implementation. The new `cli.mdx` sentence (`package.json` and its React and Tailwind dependencies, the Tailwind PostCSS plugin and CSS entry, `tsconfig.json`; reports only, changes no file) is a true summary of `runDiagnostics`' four sections; it omits the TypeScript-range and inert-`tailwind.config` findings, which is a summary, not a false claim. The pin reads the description paragraph of `doctor --help` (second blank-line-separated block), asserts it is non-empty (lit control) and that it does not match `fix`, so it pins the kind of claim, not the wording.
7. **The `serve` text correction — right.** `cli.ts` declares `--no-open` on `serve` exactly as on `dev` (`-p`, `-h`, `--no-open` on both), so the old docs line "(no `--no-open`)" was false and the new "flags as `dev`, `--no-open` included" is true. The `serve` row of the flag-contract table gains `--no-open`; green at BASE by design, a docs-to-bin alignment pin.
8. **The new `cli.mdx` "Scaffolding a plugin" line against `packages/create-plugin` — right, with one wording residue.** `packages/create-plugin/package.json` at the head names `@object-ui/create-plugin`, one bin `create-plugin` → `./dist/index.js`, `publishConfig.access: public`, no `private`, a member of the `fixed` group; npm's `create` resolves `@object-ui/plugin` to `@object-ui/create-plugin` and runs its sole bin; the bin's `program` takes `[plugin-name]`, `-d, --description` and `-a, --author`, so `NAME` on the command line is a positional it accepts; the registry answers `17.6.0` as `latest` (the dev measured a run under a pty writing `packages/plugin-probe-widget/`). The link `/docs/utilities/create-plugin` resolves to the page that carries the "run it at a pnpm workspace root" caveat the section delegates (`Internal Docs Link Check`, tally below). **Residue:** the section's sentence "A plugin is scaffolded by its own initializer, `@object-ui/create-plugin`, not by this CLI" sits in the same page as the `generate` section's example `objectui generate plugin my-widget`, and `generate.ts` at the head still writes `plugins/NAME/index.ts`, an in-app plugin stub. "A plugin package" would be exact; "not by this CLI" overstates by one word. Not an accept-set change and not a prescription that fails; named for the next `cli.mdx` toucher (carrier: the seat), not blocking — the same class as the `analyze` banner residue the objectui#11499 record named.
